newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. Defence Secretary briefs Israel counterpart.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Defence Secretary briefs Israel counterpart.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry on Saturday telephoned Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai and briefed him on developments in Iraq, an Israeli Defence Ministry spokesman said.

Perry also invited Mordechai to visit Washington in October to discuss upgrading strategic cooperation between the two countries, spokesman Avi Benayahu told Reuters. He said Mordechai would travel to the United States in mid-October.

Israel was the target of Iraqi Scud missile attacks during the 1991 Gulf War. Israelis flocked to gas mask distribution centres after the U.S. missile attacks against southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"Perry telephoned Mordechai today and updated him on the situation in Iraq and the American army's action in the area," Benayahu said.

The U.S. Defence Secretary said on Friday the United States sees "positive developments in northern Iraq" as Iraqi troops withdraw from the area, which forces entered last week to help a Kurdish group take a key city from a rival Kurdish group.

Perry reportedly will meet next week with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Netanyahu leaves for the United States on Sunday evening and will hold talks on Monday with President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Warren Christopher.
